description: Canonical registry of conformance vector identifiers. Every ak.vector.* identifier referenced by prose or fixtures MUST appear here, and every row MUST point at the prose or fixture source that defines it.

vectors.description: Personal blocklist whole-value CAS updates, target closure, shared-history receive-before-filter behavior, unblock projection rebuild and non-enumerable holder-side filtering.

Account Data keys are server-versioned compare-and-set registers: a stale byte-identical retry after a newer write is rejected with cas_conflict, concurrent delete/update elects exactly one winner, opposite arrival orders reach the same final state, the revision high-water mark survives tombstone GC so deleted values cannot be resurrected, and value_tombstone key patterns refuse physical delete.

A human Contact remark is globally keyed by peer.principal_id through an opaque holder-private HMAC/JCS suffix; petname is holder-authored, confirmed_display_name is an explicit verified PCR Profile confirmation baseline, ordinary edits preserve it, Realm/Directory fallbacks cannot initialize it, raw principal IDs, Realm IDs, pairwise actor IDs, and peer service IDs are forbidden key material, and decrypted slot swapping fails closed.

The two registered typed-id account-data namespaces are closed: ak.views.private.<view_id> and ak.notifications.inbox.<notification_id> accept only a full typed id tail, reject the bare namespace instead of falling through to the permissive unregistered-key branch, refuse plaintext content, bind the decrypted private View to visibility=private and its own view_id while the shared ak.view.* surfaces reject visibility=private, close the inbox value to dismissed/archived with an HLC-then-device_id merge, and delete physically without allowing revival.

Account Authority issuer ledger: genesis and CAS successor chaining, record identity and proof binding, the closed replica classification table, idempotency conflict and the bounded fanout outbox transitions.

Actor Profile accountability admission is deterministic: every declared principal needs an active matching grant, any missing grant rejects the whole Event, and field-stripped acceptance is non-conformant.

Byte-exact I2OSP(counter, AEAD.Nn) KAT for exporter content and Signal nonces. Non-zero high-order padding, counter rollback/reuse and increment after u64 exhaustion fail closed; no sender nonce prefix or random fallback exists.

Act-on-behalf requires an authorization_ref, live participation, matching grant scope and a single-use controller approval; approval replay fails with approval_already_consumed and unauthorised Sidecar creation fails with sidecar_create_denied.

Agent lifecycle is active/paused/deactivated with deactivated terminal: resume fails agent_deactivated, pause-while-paused fails agent_paused, one lifecycle Event carries deactivation without client-authored key or grant bundles, and deactivation becomes a mandatory AND gate over every runtime key, session, pairing handle, grant, KeyPackage and presence path within sixty seconds.

Historical Agent materialization freezes original state and tagged acceptance: the original producer proof and authorization evidence, or a distinct receiver receipt. Same selector and acceptance replay returns the original root; conflicting acceptance/root never overwrites it. Complete historical method evidence is evaluated at original proof times, independent of verifier-now expiry.

Agent key authorizations and accountability grants without expires_at stay valid until revoked; same-key re-authorization atomically replaces every observed authorization dot, concurrent re-authorizations fold to the intersection of scope and audience with the earliest finite expiry, and pause fails new sessions closed and invalidates issued ones inside a freshness window of at most sixty seconds.

Agent effective membership is bound to the exact controller authority pair and join Event generation; self leave is one complete atomic cascade, while third-party terminal removal freezes a durable exact-set cleanup intent without delaying immediate authority loss or synthesizing Agent Events.

Agent mention selectors resolve through selector_claim.subject_account_id: ambiguous or unavailable selectors fail closed, a slug change keeps the historical target, the same principal on another Station is a different account, and retargeted stations, proof reuse and expected_actor_id hints are rejected rather than used to break ambiguity.

Agent MLS KeyPackages bind exclusively to the current accepted ak.agent.key.authorize Event and its runtime signing key, never to a controller delegated-device authorization; stale, mixed, cross-principal, revoked, superseded, expired, or key-mismatched bindings fail closed.

Agent key pairing pins ak.gate.account.command.pair_agent_key.v1 and its failure set: expired pairing requests fail pairing_request_expired, and DID mismatch, invalid proof and deactivated agent each map to their own stable code.

Circle and Strand participation ceilings may only drop bits from their parent: a child enabling act_on_behalf under a disabled parent bit, or a Strand re-enabling a Circle-disabled third-party mention bit, is rejected with agent_participation_ceiling_widen.

Effective Agent participation is the bitwise meet of the current governance/deployment ceiling and the controller selection; the five selection bits are independent of requested scope, participation is an additional action gate rather than a grant, and an unknown source yields the empty set.

The Account Authority stores the full controller participation selection under compare-and-set versioning without turning it into authority: enforcement intersects the stored selection with current governance, and a capped bit grants no action and creates no capability grant.

Session scope_details.participation entries are isomorphic to agent_participation_entry and are a behavior contract, not an authorization boundary: a runtime operation without the backing capability grant still fails with failed_precondition.

With accept_third_party_mention false, non-controller mentions fan out to no agent notification, inbox entry, push or subscribe projection while the controller's own mention still delivers; enabling the bit later is non-retroactive.

Agent bootstrap is constructed in one acyclic order: controller-signed PCR-independent DID entry 0 -> exact initial_resolution -> frozen genesis create -> realm_id=retype(event_id) -> accepted provision -> accepted PCR -> controller-signed create-locked DID entry 1. Covers awaiting_pcr_genesis and awaiting_did_binding invisibility, exact durable commitment comparison, activation only after entry 1, and rejection of same-batch submission, undeclared genesis, duplicate claim, service-chosen realm id, cross-server split or wrong DID update key/tuple.
Agent DID-to-PCR binding, controller delegated authoring attribution, control-fact placement, and rejection of non-PCR Realms at either principal control id.
Agent provisioning declares its principal-control Realm id forward, before the Agent PCR genesis Event is submitted.

Agent re-pairing keeps an active or paused agent intact until pairing completes, issues one fresh handle that makes every previous handle permanently unresolvable, and applies one controller-signed authorize Event whose exact supersedes set atomically replaces every prior active authorization dot; stale, partial, extra or wrong supersedes sets fail closed without changing any key.

The public Agent DID history contains only the requested_scope commitment digest; complete scope disclosure is controller-signed, verifier/audience/challenge-bound, short-window private evidence, and public-copy, mismatch, stale, wrong-audience, and replay variants fail closed.
Stable runtime key binding digest, same-binding idempotent retry, different-binding HTTP 409 conflict, and stale approval fail-closed behavior.

Agent session issuance pins ak.gate.account.command.issue_session_grant.v1: exact replay with a fresh matching-holder DPoP returns the original grant while reused DPoP, conflicting intent, audience mismatch and bad signatures fail closed, and a missing accountability grant is pinned as accountability_grant_missing.

Executes reusable current Agent state, original same-Station or independent receiver historical admission, independent lifecycle gates, canonical witnesses, original genesis producer proof after resume, Station-admitted controller device binding, MLS cross-binding and tamper cases.

High-risk agent session scope returns claim_required with closed details {reason_code=human_approval_required, approval_request_id}; controller approval is out of band and CAPTCHA, OTP, password, and browser challenges are forbidden on the runtime path.
Request-key canonical body conflict, scope binding, canonical_hash_input and 24-hour retention semantics.

Applet-managed Bot/Ghost creation uses an exact account ActorId, independently verified method evidence, immutable provision/PCR anchors, fixed atomic units, DID namespace matching, ordinary PCR rotation and a generic registration/grant/revoke write fence.

Deterministic Applet registration_epoch recomputation from the closed normalized transcript, UTF-8 domain separator, JCS bytes, and SHA-256; covers set sorting and duplicate rejection, optional omission, DID method version evidence, and security-field rotation.

Caller-signed Applet revoke plan binding, durable pre-effect ledger bound to principal service and admin actor, exact replay, conflict rejection, non-skip partial outcomes, restart recovery, and first-accepted-event write fencing.

Applet transaction push delivery authentication record: per-delivery RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signature covering method/target/authority/content-digest/arkret-operation/source-service-id/destination-service-id/idempotency-key, receiver-derived delivery_authentication_record and its domain-separated digest are persisted into the idempotency/replay record, duplicate body/record conflicts fail closed, and source service authentication does not replace Event actor/applet/capability checks.
field_access.sensitive_fields read projection handling: redact/hash/omit remove original values, hash uses keyed/salted digest discipline, and unenforceable handling falls back to omit.

The accepted-device possession proof binds request_id, account subject, handoff digest, complete account_id, device_id, audience, holder jkt, verification method, session intent and a window of at most 300 seconds; audience mismatch fails audience_mismatch and a broken binding fails proof_invalid with issuer-fixed TTL.
Closed SessionGrant issuance preimage, typed ID/JWT jti derivation, holder/recovery binding, canonical public-JWK normalization, durable exact replay, conflict and terminal outcomes.
Two signature-valid but different Commits on one (realm_id, stream_ref, governance_generation, stream_position) freeze that stream; consumers MUST NOT pick a winner.
Realm, Circle and Sidecar streams each start and advance their own predecessor chain; planned handoff transfers every private head without exposing hidden stream existence in the public bundle.
After a planned handoff is accepted, a write signed by the old generation is rejected; only the new generation extends the stream from the imported final head.
A RealmCommit whose predecessor leaves its own stream, skips a position, or nulls a non-zero position is rejected and writes nothing.

A non-state-changing Event whose authorization_ref resolves in the committed typed state of the current governance Station is accepted and projected locally without waiting for a covering RealmCommit.
Projected writes earlier in one ordered submit batch never become the authorization basis for later Events in the same batch; dependants wait for the subsequent RealmCommit.
A state-changing Event stays pending until a valid RealmCommit on its own stream accepts it; the decision rests on the Commit itself, because v1 has no recomputed state root to appeal to.
Authority lease issuance, ordered batch delivery, exact idempotent refresh, founding anchor basis, stale/quorum failure and cache-clearing boundaries.

Executable closed WebSocket discovery and frame bytes, application-context DPoP KAT and replay binding, account/events/signal multiplex isolation, duplicate/unknown/oversize negatives, reauth, drain, close-code traces and mandatory HTTP fallback.

Streaming AEAD declared-bounds negatives (declared fields only, no multi-MiB payload materialised): segment_count above 2^20, segment_bytes below 1 KiB or above 8 MiB, and segment_count inconsistent with ceil(size_bytes / segment_bytes) MUST all be rejected fail-closed (schema_violation, reason_code segment_bounds_invalid) before key derivation or any segment download.
Streaming AEAD ordering: out-of-order / skipped / gapped segment_index MUST be rejected with segment_sequence_invalid; a repeated segment_index MUST be rejected with segment_replay.

Streaming chunked AEAD (ak.blob.stream_aead.v1) happy path: Event and proof-hash group-state refs derive the exact winning epoch without a wire epoch; multi-segment plaintext with a short final segment is split, per-segment AEAD encrypted, incrementally verified, and the top-level ciphertext_digest is recomputed. Unresolved/non-winning refs and a different derived epoch fail closed.

Streaming AEAD scheme closure: an unknown attachment scheme MUST fail closed with unsupported_attachment_scheme (no fallback decrypt); an envelope carrying both whole-file nonce and chunked nonce_prefix/segment_* fields MUST fail blob.schema.json encrypted_attachment oneOf validation.

Streaming AEAD truncation: a dropped final segment, a last segment whose flag stays 0x00, or segment_count exhausted without last_segment_flag=0x01 MUST be rejected with segment_stream_truncated and buffered plaintext discarded.

calendar.attendees is the single canonical roster: actor ids are unique, the omitted role defaults to required, at most one organizer exists, and roster membership creates no Realm or Circle membership and widens no history access.

One schedule patch derives exactly one notification per receiver over the pre/post roster union filtered by post-state access, mute, DND and push rules; encrypted schedules only produce the profile-defined blind wakeup; RSVP changes derive no schedule notification.

Calendar Strands activate exactly one way: Strand.schema_refs carries ak.schema.calendar_event.v1 and metadata.fields.calendar co-occurs in both directions on the post-patch object, the container self-schema is refused in schema_refs, flat schedule fields and metadata.fields.profile/profile_refs impostors are refused, and writes bind the schema in requirements.schema[].

Nonexistent and ambiguous local times both resolve with the offset in effect before the transition, so a fixed local meeting time does not drift across a DST boundary and the overlap emits exactly one occurrence.

RFC 8984 subset defaults, base start as the first occurrence counted against count, implicit inheritance of base time and weekday components, count/until typing and exclusivity, by_* companion preconditions, and the paginated expansion with its candidate-period scan budget and revision-bound continuation.
Excluded recurrence rules, recurrence overrides, RDATE/EXDATE, per-instance reschedule or cancellation, and the JSCalendar @type discriminator all fail closed instead of being silently ignored.

RSVP admission is capability-based rather than attendee-based, refuses cancelled events, and layers basis checks so that e2ee and plaintext Realms accept the identical canonical set: shape admission requires exactly one well-formed ak:event: typed id in entry.schedule_basis_refs and is decidable from that field alone without resolving it, target admission reads only the referenced Event plaintext envelope and pends on dependency_missing, and basis validity is projection-only. Missing, invisible, cross-Realm and non-calendar targets remain externally indistinguishable.

The instance winner overrides the series fallback without unioning the two cells, the fixed causal-register rank converges independently of arrival order and HLC, and a missing key projects encrypted_unresolved instead of fabricating a status.
RSVP occurrence key canonicalizes recurrence instance local wall-clock start in the event timezone.

The RSVP response branch follows the effective scope encryption floor: plaintext is refused under an e2ee floor, permitted only with the declared rsvp_response data class otherwise, never silently downgraded, and the routing-visible metadata set is disclosed explicitly.

ak.rsvp.set declares one deterministic reducer projection, set(payload.entry): an implementation that omits the registered write, projects an extra target, or derives a value different from the canonical payload entry fails conformance. Those writes are reducer-local output and never producer-selected Event fields.

Identity-affecting schedule edits orphan instance RSVPs and mark series RSVPs needs_reconfirmation, non-calendar updates are not schedule revisions, and concurrent schedule writes select one deterministic causal-register winner without a resolution Event.

all_day selects the date branch and its negation the whole-second LocalDateTime branch for start, end and recurrence.until; intervals are half-open so end is strictly later than start; UTC timestamps, offsets, bracketed zones and fractional seconds are refused.

Producers canonicalize Link aliases to the canonical Zone before signing, receivers refuse non-canonical signed zones, a schedule-signed tzdb_version outside the executable set fails closed, and a release bump may move derived instants without changing the signed timezone or any local occurrence key.
Call state axes project independently: each axis carries its own typed current result, and a transition on one axis never rewrites another.
Accepts the three legal first call states and rejects active or terminal first states.
Moderator kick/ban requires ak.call.moderate (call_moderation_unauthorised otherwise); the call moderation effective OR-Set gates token re-issue with call_participant_removed.
Same-basis sibling transitions to different states return fsm bottom instead of selecting a winner.

P2P calls converge to SFU when participants exceed two, reusing the oldest_membership no-vote session_focus election; mode does not auto-downgrade, and ak.call.summary is gated on a terminal call state (call_summary_invalid otherwise).

Every defective participant_binding maps to the single participant_binding_invalid code at reducer admission - unanchored issuer, tuple mismatch, expiry and signature failure alike - while a fully valid binding control is accepted.

Recording ready results MUST carry ak.schema.call_recording_artifact.v1 metadata bound to the recording start event, Arkret blob pipeline, recording exporter label/context, retention policy, deletion audit trigger, and erasure receipt.

Recording retention: audit_lock blocks deletion (legal_hold_active) regardless of retention_expires_at, and ak.call.recording.start cannot enter a capturing state without an atomically persisted consent_confirmed result.
Same-basis replay of the same from/to transition is idempotent and does not create a divergent head.
Terminal call states reject every attempted outgoing transition with call_state_terminal.

Transcription requires ak.call.transcribe (transcription_denied otherwise), and transcript artifacts MUST use the ak.rtc-transcript-key/v1 exporter label with a dedicated Context (transcription_artifact_pipeline_bypassed otherwise).
Covers every legal call lifecycle transition and representative non-terminal illegal transitions.
Profile-declared non-event grant authority permits only exact Realm-admin-to-active-bridge-registration ak.applet.ghost.provision grants and rejects owner shortcuts or binding drift.

An unmet approval constraint blocks direct execution even for a high-privilege grant: a reproducible proposal/review lifecycle is required, and approval produces a verifiable completion Event that a separate action Event then consumes.

Capability materialization preserves exact issuer and concrete-subject ActorIds, derives maximum depth plus canonical sorted and deduplicated root identities, and requires each parent subject ActorId to equal the child issuer ActorId in full. Producer-supplied derived members and same-DID cross-Station replay are rejected; missing parents remain dependency-pending and independent reducers produce the same state-root input.

A multi-level authority chain built from one grant shape: each grant records the grant it was issued under in issuer_authority_refs, and revoking an ancestor invalidates its descendants at read time without any cascading write.
Delegation cycle rejection across direct, multi-hop, revoke/redelegate and atomic batch variants.
Capability authority expiry takes effect against the committed authority instance; an expired grant fails closed even when the caller presents a locally projected view.
Direct Conversation participant authority is a profile-scoped non-grant source, survives root generation changes, requires the pair's unique immutable binding, and cannot issue child grants.
Risk-tier freshness matrix fails closed and keeps unknown low-risk pending outcomes local.
Global cross-grant decision merge prevents any allow from bypassing deny, quarantine or review.
Issuer effective-authority and freshness-unknown fail-closed checks for first-issued grants.
Static depends_on_moderation_state requirement rejects missing or false declarations.

After an accepted ak.capability.revoke of grant G, a pending Event authorized by a child grant derived from G fails closed or is quarantined with a stable reason code, allow and policy-decision cache entries depending on G or its child are invalidated in the same reducer transaction, and later snapshots and exports never present G as currently valid.
Effective grant validity-window intersection rejects empty windows.
A Circle activates on its own commit stream; Realm activation neither implies nor blocks it.

Under directory_visibility=members a Realm member outside the Circle receives exactly the locked stub an absent Circle returns - the same fixed key set and timing bucket - while a Circle member sees full metadata without changing the non-member shape.
directory_visibility=realm_members exposes only the Realm-member preview field set and gives non-Realm callers the same locked stub/timing bucket as members-only circles.

Circle lifecycle is evaluated in the source-Station serializable admission gate: admission before archive is retained, archive or tombstone before admission blocks, and restore requires a newly signed Event.

Signed Event scope_ref, projected effective_scope and Circle lifecycle admission: the producer signs the matching scope_ref, the reducer verifies it and materializes effective_scope only in read projections, and source-Station serializable ordering, archive and tombstone barriers, restore re-signing, expected_revision checks and rebind transitions all hold together with their negatives.

Revoking consent immediately invalidates the cached private contact discovery result, invite capability gate and PSI index: directory lookup stops returning the peer, the next invite submission fails its precondition and re-evaluates the gate, an any-scope revoke clears every scope cache, and the next PSI rotation excludes the peer.

A mutually signed, root-anchored bilateral checkpoint compacts an arbitrary Contact prefix while retaining a maximum 64-round explicit tail; fork, rollback, missing predecessor, wrong root/pair/accumulator and single-signature inputs fail closed, while missing material remains distinguishable from invalid material without disclosing Contact state.

The ak.self.contact.read.list.v1 projection carries the closed next_prepare_input successor cursor: an accepted row MUST carry it and the five non-authorable contact_state values MUST NOT, its contact_round_id, version and predecessor_event_ref are copied verbatim into the scope_update and tombstone prepare phases, version is the next Event's version and predecessor_event_ref is the current lineage head rather than that head's predecessor, and a stale cursor is refused with contact_lineage_conflict or contact_scope_stale and MUST be re-read rather than guessed or retried unchanged.

Own-Station verified incoming request projection includes exact request_event_ref and optional original request_message. The client submits peer/ref, checks the prepared intent and signs without resolving the request Event or verifying foreign receipts/history. The server loads durable evidence and rejects stale, wrong-holder, wrong-peer, glare and consumed slots with zero writes. Contact mirrors are never exposed through Event resolve.

Decrypted ak.contacts.actor.<principal_key> plaintext: the closed value shape, the display profile shared with the Actor Profile display name, the canonical handle wire form, and the domain half a schema cannot state -- storage-key recomputation, explicit-confirmation-only refresh of the display-name baseline, the section 3.1 tag namespace, retention across a suspended Contact, and an unreadable value never overwriting a verified local record.

Inline and long-text selection is decided on measured UTF-8 bytes without splitting a Unicode scalar: at or below the inline limit the block stays ak.content.text, above it becomes ak.content.long_text, and a fallback body over its limit is rejected with payload_too_large.

E2EE long text uses the ak.blob.stream_aead.v1 scheme with a _stream algorithm suffix and max(1,ceil(size/segment)) segments; the content counts as complete only after every segment tag and the digest verify, and whole-file scheme, non-stream algorithm, digest mismatch, reordered or truncated segments and bad media types are all rejected.

Redaction, expiry and blob-access revocation invalidate every message-derived view including the partial search index and cache, blob garbage collection runs on reference tracking, push providers never receive the full text, and mention handling never requires a server-side blob scan.

Producers normalize CRLF and bare CR to LF before digesting, BOM and forbidden control characters are rejected, Unicode normalization of the body is forbidden, and line count is zero for empty text and lf_count+1 unless a trailing LF is present.

KeyPackage upload, entry upload, minimal consume command, consume service receipt, and revoke signatures use byte-exact domain-separated typed JCS transcripts. Consume authority and all owner/KeyPackage/Welcome/service coordinates have one carrier in recipient_durable_receipt; wrapper mirrors and non-canonical selectors fail closed.

A failed or unverifiable cross-Station fetch surfaces as device_directory_unavailable and is never rendered as an omitted row, an empty device list, an expired cache hit or an extended attestation validity window.

Cross-Station device directory reads collapse absent, invisible, unrelated, revoked, fenced and policy-denied targets into one indistinguishable outcome, authorize by relationship and purpose rather than by caller assertion, and decide transport authentication before any target read.

accepted_device pairing signs a closed target-owned possession attestation under ak.device_authorize_accepted_device_possession_proof.v1 whose only replay boundary is the staged short-link pairing challenge transcript digest: the approving device and the Account Authority each rebuild it independently, it is the sole authority for hpke_key and algorithms, it travels only in the out-of-band QR or short-link fragment, transcripts never cross between root_anchored and accepted_device, and the target device fails closed before local assembly when the accepted Event does not match its attestation or the expected principal_id.

Fresh-device authorization has exactly one bootstrap transcript, ak.device-pairing.challenge.v1, tied to an account-less bounded-TTL staged request. Pair commit requires that still-pending request; stage/resolve/status expose no principal, sibling targets, or SessionGrant, and an unauthorized fresh device cannot call self device-message operations.

Device pairing is a two-phase pending request: stage stays account-less, and finalize is the one authenticated step that binds the record to an exact AccountId by attaching a target proof signed over a transcript that includes it. The eight-character code is unique across the whole live pending window, so a second stage call always mints a distinct one and is the only input of the authenticated code claim, which returns the byte-equivalent bootstrap and proof of the QR path and never a weaker code-only branch. staged advances one way to ready_for_claim, and a successful finalize supersedes every other unaccepted ready_for_claim record of the same AccountId into terminal expired in the same durable transaction, keyed by AccountId alone so a refreshed page and a different device behave identically, never rewriting an outcome pair_device already accepted and never superseding twice on an exact retry. An unknown, wrong, expired, superseded, cross-account, not yet finalized or already consumed code is indistinguishable from every other in one uniform not_found, while status still reports expired for a superseded record exactly as it does for an elapsed TTL.

document_digest is sha256:lowercase_hex(SHA-256(RFC8785_JCS(normalized DID Document projection))): any raw JSON property reordering keeps the digest identical, changing any controller / verification relationship / service / security-relevant extension property necessarily changes it, and raw response bytes are never carried in document_digest (they use raw_document_digest).

evidence_digest is recomputable from the retained canonical evidence receipt (ak.did.binding_evidence.v1): a proofless method degrades to an empty method_proofs array rather than a placeholder, webvh witness rows are sorted by witness_did with duplicates rejected, any method evidence change changes the digest, and unknown method or proof kinds fail closed.

policy_digest is recomputable from the retained canonical resolver policy snapshot (ak.did.resolver_policy.v1): required core dimensions (accepted_did_methods, fail_mode, trust_roots) plus the profile-closed profile_policy, registered wire tokens only (language-native debug renderings rejected), and flipping any security-relevant field necessarily changes the digest while unknown profiles or fields fail closed.

Byte-exact KAT for the receiver-derived off-wire Direct Conversation binding digest: fixed v1 domain separator, closed normalized binding object, unordered participant and authorization-ref normalization, created_at and Event-context exclusion, and semantic-field mutation separation.

A lost Direct Conversation founder never transfers the existing pair slot: ordinary recovery of the exact same (principal_id, station_id) resumes as the original founder, while timeout, root Contact recovery policy, third-party attestation and after-the-fact bilateral designation all write nothing. The non-founder remains awaiting_founder, the closed wire union has no founder_unrecoverable state, and only a genuinely different stable participant pair derives a new pair_key with no inherited history, MLS state, keys, audit identity or authority.

One accepted founding unit per (founder_id, trust_domain_id, pair_key) slot across same-Station, dual-Station and founder multi-device concurrency: first valid unit wins, the loser gets direct_conversation_slot_already_committed with zero writes, exact replay returns the byte-identical receipt without advancing accepted_at, the same idempotency key with a different unit is duplicate_conflict, every crash point converges to the same coordinates, and the federation branch reports a missing bounded dependency as a top-level retryable dependency_missing rather than a partial.

The creation_required resolver outcome carries next_founding_input with member names identical to the founding unit submission, exactly one founding_authority_evidence branch, no Event bytes or coordinates, temporarily_unavailable when the material cannot be assembled, and submission-side re-verification that never trusts the echoed copy.

Caller-authored first-valid founding unit: byte-exact founding_unit_digest KAT over the four ordered Event IDs, realm_id and main_strand_id retyped from the first and third Event IDs, explicit founder membership, closed self and peer carrier branch shapes, and rejection of server-allocated identifiers, reserved or materializing drafts, coordinator election, reordering, a fifth Event and a carried coordinate field.

Canonical direct-conversation pair_key KAT over exact ActorIds sorted by RFC 8785 JCS bytes and the Realm trust domain, including order-independence and bare-principal/unresolved-pairwise-DID rejection rules.

The Direct Conversation resolver reports only server-verifiable send blockers. personal_blocked and history_key_unavailable are absent from the closed wire enum because holder blocklist state is encrypted to holder devices and history key installation is device-private, so a reply carrying either value is a schema_violation; they are carried instead by the closed client-local blocker set, which never appears on any wire surface and never turns the resolver state into suspended. presence_offline and keypackage_empty remain server-verifiable but are returned only to an existing exact-pair participant, and a non-participant probe gets the same opaque failure as a nonexistent pair.
A resource outside the declared Directory accept_policy is rejected with accept_policy_denied and produces no entry, no partial state and no information about other resources.
Directory ingest rejects an announce whose governance signature does not verify, before any entry, TTL or policy_revision is established.
Directory ingest requires bidirectional opt-in: the resource must opt in to the Directory and the Directory must accept the resource; a one-sided announce establishes no entry.
An announce from a service that is not an authorized Directory writer is rejected with directory_unauthorized without revealing whether the target resource exists.
An announce whose governance signature is valid but stale relative to the accepted source_refs checkpoint is rejected with signature_stale rather than silently refreshing the entry.

Directory announce accepts only a current source-signed carrier for the authenticated Directory and exact announce, and peer exact resolve returns only requested refs inside that carrier; wrong source, wrong Directory, expiry, supersession, withdrawal and out-of-carrier selectors fail closed.

Missing, hidden and invite-only-without-proof Realm resolutions return the same 404 not_found status, body shape and timing bucket, and never leak realm_id, title, join_rule, discoverability, member_ids or service endpoints.
An operator takedown records an auditable decision, blocks the entry from further external exposure, and gives external callers a blinded response indistinguishable from absence.
An organization badge is shown only from independently verified evidence bound to the organization DID control state; unverified or expired evidence yields no badge rather than a weaker claim.
Organization search returns only entries whose discoverability admits keyword search, and every result carries the common as_of, source_refs and policy_revision fields.
The Directory never holds or returns pairwise or private persona DIDs: they are excluded from ingest, from query results and from any derived index.

An announce whose as_of predates the stored entry, or whose policy_revision derives from a checkpoint already superseded, is rejected with policy_revision_rollback; the digest itself is never compared lexicographically.
Public and listed Realms are returned by keyword search with the common freshness fields, while unlisted, invite_only and secret Realms never appear in search results.
Re-announcing the same resource state is idempotent: it refreshes the effective TTL within max_ttl_seconds without creating a second entry or advancing policy_revision on unchanged input.
resolve_agent_selector failure branches for missing, hidden, and unauthorized selectors return the same status, body shape, error class, and timing bucket.
resolve_handle failure branches for missing, hidden, and unauthorized handles return the same status, body shape, error class, and timing bucket.
Resolving a hidden target is indistinguishable from resolving a target that does not exist, in status, body shape and timing bucket.

A restricted handle or claim is returned only when the caller satisfies the registered presentation and policy gate; otherwise the account_id and claim contents are withheld rather than partially disclosed.

Every Directory result carries as_of and policy_revision, and carries a non-empty sorted duplicate-free CommittedEventRef[] source_refs whenever it has an Event source, omitting the field entirely when it has none.
A result past its TTL or contradicting the verified source_refs checkpoint is marked stale or removed, and consumers reject it instead of treating it as current.
Re-announcing a resource under an in-force takedown is rejected with takedown_in_force and the external response stays blinded.
An entry whose TTL expires without renewal is marked stale or removed, and never keeps answering queries as a current entry.

An unlisted resource stays out of keyword search but, where policy allows, resolves by exact id, alias, signed invite or source Realm edge, and a disallowed attempt fails indistinguishably from absence.
After withdrawal the entry stops answering queries and external callers receive the same blinded not_found response as for a resource that never existed.
DND uses closed canonical account data, half-open recurring wall-clock periods, explicit all-day state, fixed tzdb, deterministic DST conversion, and last-valid recovery for malformed updates.

Multiple active moderation decisions use the deterministic strictest fold instead of being mislabeled as split; require_review is carried by the active decision add and resolution atomically lifts every applicable review gate before current authz is re-evaluated or a stricter replacement is added.

realm_id is the retype of its ak.realm.create Event token; a carried or non-derived value is rejected with realm_id_not_event_derived.

Registry-parameterized collision suite applied to every id_kind_registry row whose id_form is producer_allocated. Field patches apply atomically against the declared pre-state: a partially applied patch or an unbound pre-state is rejected and the target object is left completely unchanged.
Pins the ak.schema.patch.v1 snake_case-only path grammar, 16-segment inclusive boundary, 1024-byte inclusive boundary, and patch_path_invalid rejection without parser fallback.

Preview authority exposes only the registered stripped projection with no history events and no exporter secrets, never creates current membership or committed-history eligibility, and makes unknown, expired and wrong-scope tokens outwardly indistinguishable.

Transcript KAT for ak.event_proof.v1: digest input deletes exactly `event_id`, `proofs`, `unsigned`; canonical binding bytes, detached JWS, and the same unsigned body replayed under ak.extension_manifest_proof.v1 rejected.
Private contact discovery returns set membership only: it never exposes reachability, provider routing, presence or any other metadata about the queried identifiers.
Private contact discovery keeps the fixed two-round blind/match OPRF shape bound to the advertised key epoch, and a request that collapses or reorders the rounds is refused rather than answered.

The wire batch cardinality equals the advertised batch_item_count rather than the real identifier count, evaluated elements and derived prefixes keep the same length and order as the blinded input, a single batched DLEQ proof verifies under the described public key, and the result count never reveals the match count.

Quota exhaustion in the blind phase returns 429 psi_quota_exhausted as a padded Class-B problem whose maximal string projection is fixed, so the denial reveals neither the real batch contents nor which phase-specific condition fired.
An authorized broadcast mention delivers under the mentions_only watch level with reason_code watch_allows, and a plain directed mention needs no blind wakeup once local evaluation has run.

ak.device.push_route uses the actor-private server_revision_cas family for create, whole-value rotation and a secret-free revoked tombstone. Missing or stale expected_revision, concurrent siblings and old exact replay fail closed; privacy GC erases old target/provider material while retaining the revision high-water mark.

ak.edge.push.command.notify.v1 returns one outcome per input device: every notification.devices[] device_id appears in outcomes[] exactly once, none missing, none duplicated, none unrequested, and a target-level failure is expanded per device instead of collapsing into a second response shape. accepted/duplicate forbid caller resend; only a rejected outcome carrying retry_after_ms, and only for the two registered caller-retryable reasons, transfers the next attempt to the caller. Provider delivery state, provider message ids and raw push tokens never appear in the response.

A trusted public Gateway accepts only authenticated Station-to-Gateway registration handoff. Registration identities are immutable and source-tenant scoped; exact replay returns the original signed durable receipt, different content conflicts, revoked is terminal, a successor atomically tombstones its exact predecessor, and wrong source/destination/device/target or cross-tenant access fails before route mutation. Provider tokens stay inside the source Station tenant and never enter logs, receipts, notify, metrics, traces or cross-tenant indexes.
Strand-engaged here-style updates map to receiver-side mention semantics, deliver under the mentions_only watch level, and keep the shared core reason_code watch_allows.

Concurrent reaction add and remove converge on remove, a reaction never revives after redaction, a reaction across MLS epochs stays bound to its target Event and scope, and after a capability revoke new reactions from that actor fail closed while existing ones remain as historical facts.
Byte-level reaction routing HMAC KAT covering RFC 9420 exporter derivation, NFC normalization, combining code points, emoji modifiers, and cross-label/Realm/epoch negatives.

Multi-device read cursor merge is causal-first: a causally dominating position wins even when its HLC is lower, HLC max decides only causally concurrent positions, device_id breaks equal HLCs, and an undecidable causal closure stays provisional.

Realm Link transition contract: all declared initial states and transitions are accepted, tombstoned is terminal except byte-equivalent replay, undeclared transitions reject with realm_link_invalid_transition, competing same-revision transitions are serialized and stale commands reject without changing the confirmed state, general graph cycles remain valid, and self-reference rejects with realm_link_self_reference.

The ak.realm.organization payload validates against its closed schema and its two independent authorization layers: Realm-side acceptance by an admin writer or an allowed create-bootstrap batch, and Organization-side consent whose proof verifies to the organization DID control state, a threshold quorum or a registered delegation.

An event-targeted ak.redaction (target_ref in ak:event: form) only trims that Event's fields per preserve[] and MUST NOT change any object's state, including the event-derived object minted from a targeted create Event; object state=redacted is driven only by the object typed-id spelling of target_ref. The two spellings of one 33-octet token are both schema-valid and stay two distinct verbatim scalar subjects (encoding.md 9.5.1); neither spelling canonicalizes into the other.
Hard erasure produces a signed receipt and a conforming stub that carries no plaintext fingerprint, and an active legal hold blocks the erasure instead of producing a receipt.

Message reaches state=redacted only through the object-scoped ak.message.redact. The cross-object ak.redaction payload class excludes Message mechanically: message_id is not a member and target_ref removes the ak:message: branch, so both spellings fail schema validation before any typed current result write, while a non-Message object target and the ak.message.redact positive both validate.
Policy-scoped redaction strips content while retaining the timeline position and the quarantine fingerprint, so the gap remains verifiable without recovering the removed content.
Only the fields named in preserve[] survive a redaction; every other field of the target is removed, and a preserve entry outside the target's schema is rejected rather than ignored.
Snapshot pruning and backfill keep the verification stub for redacted material, so a consumer can still verify continuity without the removed content being recoverable.
The redaction payload schema accepts an ak:space: target_ref and rejects malformed target spellings, so Space redaction targets are validated structurally rather than by string matching.

Strand state=redacted forbids both its Description pair (content / encrypted_content) and tracks.synthesis content pair; Morph forbids its content pair. An object carrying any applicable slot alongside state=redacted MUST fail its schema, the redact post-state with all slots absent MUST validate, and state=archived MUST keep the slots legal.

ak.relation.resolve is the single registered carrier that settles one Relation primary conflict domain: retain_candidate keeps exactly one covered candidate with its original RelationId, while void_all leaves no active edge for the covered set and preserves the facts. Every resolution binds the complete frozen baseline; missing, duplicate, superseded or foreign members reject the whole submission. The inline diagnostic may carry at most sixteen candidates, while larger sets use the same complete paged carrier. Concurrent resolutions retain every Event identity and select one deterministic winner by (depth,EventId); a later authorized resolution references that winner and produces a higher-depth successor. Newly discovered Relation candidates outside the frozen baseline restore require_review as an explicit cross-domain check.

Relation is the only patch-surface object whose schema declares effective_scope, so it is the only place an actor could still supply the reducer-materialized value. Both surfaces MUST be decided by schema and MUST produce zero projection writes: an ak.relation.create carrying payload.relation.effective_scope, and an ak.relation.update whose patch addresses effective_scope or any effective_scope.* descendant, both fail with schema_violation reason=effective_scope_reducer_managed.

A locked existing cross-Realm target and a nonexistent target produce identical caller shapes with no forbidden target metadata, raw backfill and federation views are redacted equally, p95 timing stays within the 50ms bucket, and auditor-level access never changes the shape the ordinary caller sees.

Batch count and canonical byte limits are conjunctive: a request at both limits is accepted when every item is individually valid, byte overflow returns payload_too_large, count overflow returns schema_violation, and partial acceptance is forbidden.
A self events batch above the registered item limit is rejected with schema_violation as a whole and never partially accepted.
Capability constraint cardinality stays within the schema-defined default of 64 and an unknown critical constraint fails closed rather than being ignored as an unrecognised extension.
A Realm above 1000 active Circles rejects the next create with failed_precondition and reason_code circle_count_exceeded, leaving state unchanged.

Every non_streaming_json operation rejects a request or response carrying Content-Encoding with HTTP 415 unsupported_content_encoding, before the body is read or decompressed, and never reuses param_invalid for it.
Generated decoded-cursor, selector canonical JSON, selector term, unknown-field and policy-array boundary cases.
A complete producer-signed Event whose canonical JSON exceeds 1 MiB is rejected with payload_too_large, measured on canonical bytes rather than on transport framing.
Event refs[role=authorized_by] stays within its limit of 64 entries and the overall refs[] within 128, and an over-limit Event is rejected whole rather than truncated to fit.

Size limits are enforced while the body streams in: header bounds, body-free authentication, Content-Encoding rejection, Content-Length precheck and incremental wire-byte counting all run before JSON parsing, so an oversized body is never fully buffered or parsed first.
A single header value above 8 KiB or an aggregate header block above 32 KiB is rejected at the header boundary, before any body is read and before body-dependent authentication.
Registered per-object control cardinality limits are enforced at admission, and an over-limit control payload is rejected whole with its registered code instead of being clipped.
A canonical operation body above 8 MiB is rejected with payload_too_large, independently of the 16 MiB HTTP message content bound and the 1 MiB single-Event bound.

Generated boundary and injected-clock cases for the registered protocol windows: invite locator TTL and active count, authority commit predecessor_ref, compaction commit covered digests, device message expiry, push routes, contact request pending TTL, erasure and deactivation propagation windows, MLS deactivation grace, call empty timeout, push target mapping retention and third-party invite replay TTL.
Unsigned read-projection material is bounded by its own registered ceiling, so a large derived projection is refused or paged rather than allowed to exceed the operation body limit.
Event refs[] is capped at 128 typed business references and an over-limit Event is rejected as a whole; there are no predecessor or actor-chain refs to spill into.
A relation chain at depth 32 is fully expanded; a 33-level chain stops before reading level 33 and exposes a Lazy Link boundary instead of performing unbounded traversal.

Official SDKs expose orthogonal closed outer submission and payload-protection types, compile-fail invalid combinations, and serialize verified values through the same canonical schema/transcript used by service admission.
SDK pagination continues solely from has_more, independent of item count.
SDK computes max(server_hint_delay, jitter(local_backoff_delay)); zero, short or elapsed hints never accelerate the local ladder, and long hints are never clamped into an earlier retry.
An SDK conformance claim validates against its schema and its semantic outcome, so a claim that parses but overstates the verified surface is rejected with its registered reason code.
Blind-index stale postings after revocation, visibility tightening, redaction, expiry, or epoch rotation MUST not produce unauthorized recall.
Search hit is not an authorization proof; unauthorized or unverifiable hits return non-enumerating stubs.
Directory search, privacy-preserving search, and bridge interop surfaces stay separated and do not leak private plaintext.

RecoveryTransaction create freezes the exact unsigned first-generation recovery unit without any recovery effect, and the single client-attested commit_recovery_unit step accepts the closed RecoveryTerminalCommit - whose wire content is only the replacement-device-signed recovery_receipt, with no RealmCommit, authority signature or precomputed commit id - so that both recovery Events, their two RealmCommits at consecutive positions of the same PCR Realm stream, the generation advance, the replacement device projection, the consumed session and the completed terminal result all become observable in one atomic commit.
Recovery A/B and SecurityRotation crash, response-loss, restart, exact/conflicting replay, staged-secret loss, terminal replay and multi-backup-kind erase ordering.

The shared RFC 9421 freshness window at every edge it states: an at-ceiling lifetime accepted and an over-ceiling one rejected, zero and negative lifetimes rejected, both created-skew bounds inclusive and one second past either bound rejected, a signature rejected at the moment it reaches expires, and a byte-identical replay rejected by the time checks after the replay cache evicted it. Missing or non-integer created/expires fail before any comparison. The RFC 9449 DPoP iat/jti window is a separate contract with its own bounds and never inherits the RFC 9421 lifetime ceiling.

Generic ServiceDescribe, Applet ping, and the identity-role ServiceDescribe endpoint inspect the protocol-family bootstrap discriminator before typed v1 claims, route caching, capability intersection, or business traffic; unsupported canonical strings and malformed discriminators remain distinct failures.

Production current-v1 SessionGrant presentation has one wire scheme: Authorization: DPoP plus the matching DPoP proof. Authorization: Bearer carrying ak.session.grant is rejected even when another proof header is present; a DPoP proof outside its replay window is rejected.
A DPoP/RFC 9421 grant-binding session key must not reuse bytes, fingerprints, thumbprints, or key identifiers from the long-term device identity key; reuse fails closed.

DPoP htu binds scheme, authority, and path: cross-authority/scheme reuse, untrusted forwarding headers, and missing authority are rejected; only a configured trusted proxy with scrubbed headers may reconstruct the external URI.

Client RFC 9421 session PoP binds the operation selector. A request whose Arkret-Operation header is present and valid but absent from Signature-Input fails the coverage check with http_signature_invalid; a request whose covered selector is replaced after signing fails signature verification. The conditional components fail the same way when their trigger holds: content-digest on a request with a body, idempotency-key when the request is idempotency-keyed, x-arkret-wait-for when the header is present.

Sender-constrained session PoP: a write request with a valid RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signature (kid = current grant session_public_key, covering @method/@target-uri/@authority/content-digest) is accepted; a signature whose transcript mismatches the method/path/body digest fails verification and is rejected per api-conventions.md section 3.2 and service-http-binding.md section 2.5.

Human returning-device issue and human refresh require a current accepted-device possession proof bound to the exact intent and verified in the same current-authorization linearization; non-current device states produce zero grants.
Runtime producer and controller consumer bind exchange identity only to the accepted request Event id and reject message, local-intent and unaccepted identities.
Same-sequence request and control siblings choose the bytewise maximum canonical accepted Event envelope digest, never Event id, HLC, arrival or database order.
Controller-only complete pagination and structural Event pairing recover private Sidecar context locators without adding a disclosure endpoint.

An owned Agent without a published KeyPackage is in desired_agent_ids but outside effective access with access_readiness=key_material_pending and no plaintext branch; it gains only post-join epoch keys through the Sidecar Welcome, and once deactivated or out of the Realm it leaves the derived desired set, addressing and delivery stop immediately, a durable MLS removal obligation is created, and its later proofs, writes and queries fail closed.

Concurrent prepare and create for one (realm_id, controller_account_id) converge on a single Sidecar whose sidecar_id is the winning create event_id retyped, callers may not supply or overwrite it, a mutated draft conflicts with zero writes while the exact draft replays idempotently, and context attach only projects the (sidecar_id, source_context_ref) mapping without creating a Circle, membership, Strand or Relation.

Explicit response closed loop with runtime addressed/self eligibility and restart dedupe gates, coordinator completion policy, causal request refs, controller validation, fail-closed non-echo handling, and controller-authored durable close control.

Containment: plaintext or shared-scope occurrences of exchange binding/control schema ids or exchange_id are hard rejects/invalid; publish output, Account Data, and public/shared surfaces carry no exchange material.

Event-fold and local-cache recovery: rebuild from accepted private history, fold validation, no Account Data merge, controller-controlled ordering and sibling resolution, terminal absorption, reassignment, action-by-response-set mapping, and projection schema state invariants.

To a caller who is neither the controller nor one of its owned Agents, the account Event stream yields zero Events referencing the Sidecar native scope, no protocol Relation enumerates Sidecars or their source-context mappings, the Realm directory has no hit for sidecar_id or controller mapping, Sidecar Events raise no notification for source Strand participants, and they appear in Realm commit metadata only as opaque commitments.
Only explicit controller confirmation creates one allowlisted ordinary shared Event, with zero private identifiers, history or locators.

Context attach establishes only the source-context mapping and rejects extra track or message fields under the closed schema; the local echo projection rebuilds without duplicating requests or Agent executions, orders after the last seen shared position by stable key, keeps the main Strand title, breadcrumb and track tabs visible in both modes, shows an empty state instead of falling back to shared read/write, and admits only requests and explicit user-facing responses into the echo.
Chrome and Edge execute the hosted multi-track, multi-mode, multi-device, multi-Agent and responsive UI matrix with preserved state and incremental switching evidence.

The Sidecar participant set is exactly the controller plus the current Realm-scoped desired_agent_ids with a sorted deduplicated authority transcript digest equal to participant_authority_digest; exactly one genesis wins through Station admission and compare-and-set, the server generates no MLS private state, forges no GroupInfo or ratchet-tree digest and offers no bootstrap endpoint bypassing Event proof, and every binding mutation fails closed.

Desired membership, a delivered Welcome and a claimed KeyPackage are each insufficient alone and any incomplete combination stays pending; only an accepted Add Commit, a matching accepted Welcome referencing it, and that device consuming the same claim on an authenticated session together make the device effective, and other devices of the same principal gain nothing automatically.

When an Agent publishes, actor_id and executed_by are a single Agent DID with no group-style composite attribution; publishing content covered only by another Agent's grant, or without a fresh approval, fails closed, while its own grant lets it publish independently under its single DID.
Every shared list, expansion, activity, export, URL, log and telemetry surface discloses no Sidecar locator, identity, content or fold input.
Accepted Agent revoke, pause or deactivate immediately stops new delivery, execution and writes without implicitly terminating exchanges.
Sidecar union history exposes a checkpoint bounded by the controller's own eligibility; it never widens historical visibility beyond the effective access of the requesting principal.

Signal source and recipient authenticate current exact-account device authority independently of the Realm/scope seal_ref; destination authenticates peer source/body, sender routing and outer proof transcript/digest, scope/membership/action/TTL/MLS basis without a remote device directory or producer signature check. Cover source/recipient rejection of revoked/fenced/conflicted authority even before leaf Remove, wrong Station or key/authorization leaf binding, missing/stale recipient trust, source outbound freshness, and well-formed forged producer signatures relayed by a malicious source but rejected by the recipient. Destination with no remote directory still relays eligible items; wrong source projection and malformed transcript/digest fail closed with the proper opaque item versus request error boundary. No synthetic device identity is allowed for Agent/minimal endpoints.

Byte-level ak.history-v1 -> ak.signal-v1 ExpandWithLabel KAT for per-sender-device SignalEnvelope AEAD keys, including JCS({sender_device_id}), distinct valid-device keys under a forced equal nonce, and label/context/device/epoch negative mutations.
Encrypted Message preview keyframe/delta/abort state machine, identity derivation, attempt fork handling, resource limits, and direct final binding.
A single-hop encrypted Signal relay is accepted without writing a durable Event, without advancing any producer revision or Realm stream head, and without rewriting the relayed envelope.

Signal payload_sequence is a durable per-device/per-canonical-scope u64 high-water: forward gaps from reservation/crash/failure are accepted, repeat or rollback is stale, exact envelope replay is diagnosed separately, and scopes remain independent.

One ak.strand.tracks.update patches tracks atomically: switching the primary within a single Event never exposes an intermediate projection with two or zero is_primary=true, enable/disable and profile updates land in the same typed current update, a violating Event is rejected with schema_violation leaving tracks unchanged, and unregistered TrackNames are rejected rather than created from regex shape.
Own-Station account aggregate stream: per-stream tail continuity, durable cursor checkpoints, projection-before-checkpoint ordering, reconnect reset vs resume, and explicit delivery cancellation.
Canonical filter/query-scope cursor binding and cross-scope replay rejection.
Opaque delivery ack token, monotonic cumulative acknowledgement, binding rejection and lost escalation.
Deterministic limited-timeline window-start state basis with safe omission on unresolved bases.

DeviceMessageEnvelope requires a sender-assigned device_message_id; unacknowledged byte-identical redelivery executes durable handler effects once, conflicting reuse fails with duplicate_conflict/device_message_id_conflict, and distinct ids remain distinct logical messages.

Shared View removal is an ak.view.update patch setting state=tombstoned, so that patch MUST be accepted; state_changed_at is reducer-derived and an actor-supplied value MUST be rejected. The acceptance half is the load-bearing one: a shared View has no tombstone Event kind, so that patch IS the removal path, and while the reducer-managed path registry was read as one flat set the write could not be registered at all. The vector was description-only until view-write-contract-fixture.json gave it two executable faces: cases[] validates every payload shape against the live schemas and the live allowed_paths, and admission_cases[] pins the outcomes schema validation cannot express -- the admitted transition, the terminal gate on later update and reconcile, the refusal of an unset or an unregistered state, the refusal of an update or reconcile of a View no registered create ever wrote, shared -> private, a stale expected_state_digest that MUST NOT be resolved against an older matching value, an exact retry that produces no second effect, and a mixed patch that stores nothing. The fixture also pins the spelling: a patch map's keys ARE its paths, so the removal patch is {"state": "tombstoned"} and a {"set": {...}} wrapper is a patch on a member named `set` that no allowed_paths entry admits.

Joining a decrypting conference is refused and no media key is published when Realm policy has not authorized media-service decryption, when the SFU service DID is absent from plaintext_visible_services, or when the required plaintext warning was not shown; the first two fail with media_plaintext_service_not_authorised and the third with an equivalent stable code.
